What to look for in motorcycle boots

  • Ankle protection. Rigid ankle cups and a torsion-control sole protect the joints most at risk in a fall.
  • Waterproof membrane. Your feet sit lowest on the bike — a Gore-Tex or equivalent liner is essential in the UK.
  • Walk test them. Touring means walking too — choose a sole flexible enough for castles, pubs and fuel stops.
  • Break them in. Wear new boots around the house and on short rides before committing to a big tour.

Frequently asked questions

How much should I spend on motorcycle boots?

Our catalogue spans £143.99 to £566.99. Budget options under £150 cover the essentials, the £150–£400 mid-range hits the sweet spot for most UK tourers, and premium picks above £400 add refinement, lighter materials and longer-term durability.

Which brands are worth considering?

Popular, well-reviewed brands in this category include Alpinestars, Sidi, Eleveit, RST. All are stocked by SportsBikeShop with UK warranty support.

Do I really need waterproof kit?

In the UK, yes. Cold, wet hands and feet impair control and concentration within minutes. A waterproof membrane is one of the best touring upgrades you can make.

faq.q: Which boot type suits UK touring?
faq.a: A sport-touring boot such as the Alpinestars SMX-6 V3, or a waterproof riding shoe like the CR-X Drystar, balances protection, weatherproofing and walking comfort. Full race or motocross boots protect more but are stiff and impractical for walking around at stops.

faq.q: Do I really need motorcycle-specific boots?
faq.a: Yes. Ankle rollover and crushing are common injuries in a fall, and trainers offer no ankle support, anti-twist shank or toe protection. Even an entry boot like the RST Tractech Evo D3O at £143.99 dramatically improves safety over ordinary footwear.

Snug at the heel with toes just clear of the end and no side-to-side movement. Stiff race boots ease slightly with wear. Try them with your riding socks, and check you can still operate the gear lever and rear brake comfortably.

Not all. Race and MX boots such as the Tech 10 prioritise protection over waterproofing. For dry feet in UK weather pick a boot with a membrane, like the Alpinestars CR-X Drystar, or check the product page for a stated waterproof lining.
